diagram.title: PerfMan · Product capability map
diagram.question: Which product domains make up the managed testing workflow?

nodes.label: Workspace & access
nodes.subtitle:
Projects and membership
Admin / Engineer / Operator / Viewer
Project + tag policies
Session and audit history

nodes.label: Scenario authoring
nodes.subtitle:
Simple request journeys
JavaScript modules + lifecycle
JMX plans + thread groups
VU / RPS / ramp / spike profiles

nodes.label: Data & configuration
nodes.subtitle:
CSV parameters and partitions
Environment variables + secrets
Protocol bundles and script modules
JMX and plugin dependencies

nodes.label: Resource fleet
nodes.subtitle:
Groups, regions and capacity
Workers, clusters and Pods
Probe, drain and disconnect
Simulated group autoscaling

nodes.label: Run orchestration
nodes.subtitle:
Queue and capacity admission
Regional shards + start barrier
Lease, heartbeat and cancellation
Frozen bundles + resource release

nodes.label: Monitoring & investigation
nodes.subtitle:
Request / latency / error series
Service, script and region views
Samples, extraction, checks and logs
Worker allocation and utilization

nodes.label: Quality & reporting
nodes.subtitle:
Consecutive-window SLA rules
Protection stops and notifications
Baselines and report comparison
JSON / CSV / print-to-PDF

nodes.label: Scheduling & recording
nodes.subtitle:
Once or cron with IANA timezones
Pinned scenario + occurrence history
HAR import and managed capture
Convert captured traffic to a test

nodes.label: Operations & governance
nodes.subtitle:
Audited virtual Pod terminal
Contacts, delivery inbox and retry
People, tags and integrations
English / Chinese preferences

constraints: Nine implemented management domains, grouped by user task
Default infrastructure and network protocol traffic use managed simulation
Each organization is a separate workspace database; no cross-organization SaaS tenancy
